research_question: Can local receiver consistency be compiled into a safe, cheaper global-workspace coherence test, and is a sheaf/global-section framing materially novel or merely established CSP/database/distributed-systems theory?

sources.title: A Sheaf-Theoretic Characterization of Tasks in Distributed Systems
sources.finding: Global consistency of local computations can be expressed through global sections; cohomology can encode obstructions.

sources.title: Consistency, Acyclicity, and Positive Semirings
sources.finding: For the studied relation families, pairwise consistency implies global consistency exactly on acyclic attribute hypergraphs; cyclic scopes admit local/global gaps.

sources.title: Structure and Complexity of Bag Consistency
sources.finding: Acyclic schemas retain local-to-global consistency; cyclicity can change global consistency complexity substantially.

sources.title: Local consistency as a reduction between constraint satisfaction problems
sources.finding: Local-consistency algorithms are a substantial established CSP technique, not a novel ATOMIC invention.

sources.title: Incremental Updates of Generalized Hypertree Decompositions
sources.finding: Structural decompositions can be reused and incrementally updated; topology-aware solving has practical precedent.

sources.title: Soft and Constrained Hypertree Width
sources.finding: Practical query performance depends on decomposition properties beyond minimum width; planner choice must be benchmarked rather than inferred from theory alone.

sources.title: A Sheaf Framework for Strategic Multi-Agent Systems: From Consensus to Nash Equilibria
sources.finding: Sheaf/global-section constructions have already been proposed for heterogeneous autonomous multi-agent coordination; generic sheaf-for-agents novelty therefore collapses.

sources.title: A global workspace in language models
sources.finding: Claude exhibits a model-native J-space with workspace-like causal properties in the reported experiments; this strengthens the need to keep model-native workspace evidence separate from explicit Clay GWT semantics.

counterevidence: The core local-to-global theorem family is established prior art.
Topology/decomposition-based solver selection is established algorithmic practice.
Sheaf language has already entered distributed and multi-agent systems research.
Therefore SWC cannot be promoted as a world-first mathematical mechanism from this search.
search_scope_limitations: This was not an exhaustive patent, closed-source, standards or all-language literature search.
No claim of global novelty is authorized.
No Frank target-runtime trace benchmark was found externally because SWC is project-specific.
